sections.title: 3.2.2.1 CS_Validate
sections.text_preview: The `CS_Validate` command will validate that the format and checksum of a sequence file are correct without executing any commands in the file. This allows operators to validate a file prior to execut

sections.title: 3.2.2.2 CS_Run
sections.text_preview: The `CS_Run` command will execute a sequence. If a prior sequence is still running, it will be canceled. If a command returns a failed status, the sequence will be aborted.

sections.title: 3.2.2.3 CS_Cancel
sections.text_preview: The `CS_Cancel` command will cancel an existing sequence. If there is no sequence currently executing, the command will emit a warning event but not fail.

sections.title: 3.2.2.4 CS_Manual
sections.text_preview: The `CS_Manual` command will put the sequencer in a manual stepping mode, where the commands will be advanced by the `CS_Step` command. After entering this mode, the operator should issue a `CS_Run` c

sections.title: 3.2.2.5 CS_Start
sections.text_preview: The `CS_Start` command will execute the first command in the sequence in manual mode.

sections.title: 3.2.2.6 CS_Step
sections.text_preview: The `CS_Step` command will execute subsequent commands after receiving the `CS_Start` command.

sections.title: 3.2.2.7 CS_Auto
sections.text_preview: The `CS_Auto` command will change the sequencing mode from manual to automatic, which means that the sequencer will automatically execute commands upon loading. This command can only be run when there

sections.title: 3.2.3.1 schedIn
sections.text_preview: The `schedIn` port checks to see if there is a timed command pending. If the timer for a pending command has expired, the command is dispatched. If there is a command being executed, the command timeo

sections.title: 3.2.3.2 cmdResponseIn
sections.text_preview: The `cmdResponseIn` port is called when a command in a sequence is completed. If the command status is successful, the next command in the sequence is executed.

sections.title: 3.2.3.3 seqRunIn
sections.text_preview:
This port takes a single argument `filename` of type `Fw::String`. In
general, sending `filename` on this port has the same  effect as issuing
a `CS_Run` command with `filename` as the file name argum

sections.title: 3.2.3.4 pingIn
sections.text_preview: The `pingIn` port is called by the `Svc::Health` component to verify that the `CmdSequencer` thread is still functional. The handler simply takes the provided code and calls the `pingOut` port.
